items.prompt: Is the white knight on e5 standing on an outpost square? An outpost square is on the 4th, 5th or 6th rank counted from your own side, has no pawn on it, is defended by one of your pawns, and no enemy pawn can attack it now or by advancing (this item ignores pawn captures that would move a pawn to another file).

claims.statement: The outpost squares for White that hold one of its pieces are exactly none.
e5 is not a hole in Black's camp: a black pawn can still attack it.
The white pawn on d4 defends e5.

hints: Check whether a white pawn defends e5.
Then check the black pawns on the neighbouring files: could one of them still advance to attack e5?
Both conditions must hold for an outpost.
items.explain: The black pawn on f7 is on a neighbouring file and has not yet passed the rank from which it attacks e5, so it could still come to attack the white knight by advancing (blockers are ignored): e5 is not an outpost square. Only the black f-pawn differs from the paired position.
